Envelope, front side (copy)

Sender: Hagenbuch Trading Ltd, Aarau

Postal label: R  Registered

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the notice or the claim state that the landlord terminated because the tenant did not pay overdue rent or accessory charges within a time limit the landlord had set?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the claim state that the tenant is married or in a registered partnership and that the rented dwelling serves as the family home?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Has the landlord given the tenant notice terminating the lease of the dwelling, and has it reached the tenant?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord gave notice because the tenant had, in good faith, asserted claims under the lease (for example demanded repair of a defect or contested the rent)?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the tenant seek an extension of the lease because having to leave by the end date would be a hardship for the tenant or the tenant's family?

text:
Hello,

I'm trying to work out why Hagenbuch Trading Ltd suddenly wants us out. At the end of January 2026 I wrote to Ms Ruth Fankhauser asking them to fix the bathroom extractor fan, which had been broken since the autumn, and to look at the damp patch spreading above the shower. I also asked whether the rent could be reduced until it was done. It was a polite letter about a real problem. Ten weeks later the termination arrived. My gut says the two are connected, but I can't prove it. The notice itself says nothing on the subject, I asked Ms Fankhauser in May to tell me the reason, and she wrote back that she would "come back to me" once she had spoken to the owner. That's where it rests.

I've attached a copy of the envelope it came in, with the registered-mail sticker.

My husband Mark Huber and I have been married since 2023, and the flat at Schulhausstrasse 6 in Aarau is our home together. We moved in as a married couple in spring 2024 and it's where our whole family life happens.

The notice was sent by registered post, addressed to me, and I collected it from the post office myself in April. So there is no doubt it reached me.

The lease is attached too, so you can see the notice periods.

I'd like to know whether we have grounds to challenge the termination.

Kind regards,
Felix Walsh
